exposure: fatty acid composition in human milk
outcome: Fatty acid composition of human milk
cohort: Mother-infant pairs from the Norwegian Human Milk Study birth cohort (n = 789)
finding: Medium-chain saturated fatty acids in human milk were inversely associated with infant growth, while monounsaturated fatty acids, particularly oleic acid, were associated with an increased odds of rapid growth.
mod_finding: This study on fatty acid composition of breast milk included mode of delivery as a factor in its analysis but did not report any specific findings related to mode of delivery.
